description: Versioned host-side sensor/module descriptor format (ROADMAP.md:554, v0.5.1 T15). Maps every services/driver_catalog.h driver_id compiled into this firmware image to its connection constraints, default channel template, units, and wiring information, for a host tool (a configurator, a validation script, or a human) to consult before writing a configuration. This data is host-side only and is not executable firmware code -- it must never be treated as authoritative over the firmware's own driver_catalog.c/native_*_source_is_valid() validation, which always has the final say at configuration-apply time. static/tools/test_driver_descriptors_contract.py keeps this file's driverId set in sync with services/driver_catalog.h.

drivers.name: internal_temp
drivers.wiring: RP2350 internal die temperature sensor (ADC channel 4 on RP2350B); no external pins.

drivers.name: adc_voltage
drivers.wiring: RP2350B external ADC inputs ADC0..ADC3 (GPIO40..GPIO43 on RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1, ADC_BASE_PIN=40). ADC4..ADC7 exist on the same peripheral but are not reachable through this channel-driver path -- see the raw-diagnostic-only native_adc_voltage_read_raw() note below.

sourceIndex.note: channel-driver path only; ADC4..ADC7 are reachable only via native_adc_voltage_read_raw(), a raw diagnostic query with no channel/driver_catalog exposure at all (v0.5.1 T12, services/board_diagnostics_service.c)

drivers.name: gpio_input
drivers.wiring: Any RP2350 GPIO not otherwise reserved -- see HARDWARE_MVP.md's frozen GPIO map for RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 reservations before choosing a pin.

sourceFlags.note: pullUp and pullDown are mutually exclusive

drivers.name: gpio_output
drivers.wiring: Any RP2350 GPIO not otherwise reserved -- see HARDWARE_MVP.md's frozen GPIO map for RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 reservations before choosing a pin.

drivers.name: ads8688
drivers.wiring: RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 industrial 8-channel SPI ADC (ADS8688IDBTR), AI0..AI3 wired to CH0..CH3 on this board, CH4..CH7 tied to AGND. Shares the board's single physical SPI bus (SCK/MOSI/MISO) with ad5422 and max22190; has its own dedicated chip-select pin and uses SPI mode 1 (CPOL=0, CPHA=1), applied per transaction. See docs/datasheets/ADS8688-register-notes.md.

sourceIndex.note: AI0..AI3; the chip has 8 mux inputs, but CH4..CH7 are grounded on this board and rejected

sourceFlags.note: only these five range codes are implemented -- see the register notes for the full range table

drivers.name: ad5422
drivers.wiring: RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 2x AD5422BREZ analog-output channels (AO0/AO1), daisy-chained on the board's single physical SPI bus in SPI mode 0; no per-device chip-select, both devices share one LATCH line. Write-only: neither DAC's SDO reaches BOARD_SPI_MISO, so there is no SPI self-test; faults surface on the shared BOARD_FAULT_N line. The first channel start resets both DACs, daisy-chains them and then raises AO_ENABLE_REQ (GPIO9, claimed shared) to release the hardware CLEAR; output enable writes REXT=1 (external 15.0 kOhm RSET). See docs/datasheets/AD5422-register-notes.md.

sourceIndex.note: AO0/AO1, this board's two daisy-chained devices

sourceFlags.note: the two ranges this board qualifies (HARDWARE_MVP.md section 3.2); every other R[2:0] code is rejected -- bipolar ranges need a negative rail the board does not have

drivers.name: max22190
drivers.wiring: RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 MAX22190ATJ+ industrial digital-input frontend, DI0..DI3 wired on this board (IN1..IN4 on the chip). Shares the board's single physical SPI bus; has its own dedicated chip-select pin. Interface Mode 0 only (24-bit frame, mandatory CRC-5, no daisy chain) -- hardware pin-strapped, not software-selectable -- on SPI clock mode 0 (CPOL=0, CPHA=0), applied per transaction. The first channel start runs HARDWARE_MVP.md's frozen chip initialization (INEN=0x0F, FLT1..FLT4=0x04, CFG=0x01, WB/FAULT2 cleared, FAULT2EN=0x3C, GPO=0x80, FAULT1EN=0xF8, POR cleared, all read back). See docs/datasheets/MAX22190-register-notes.md. CRC-5 follows ADI's MAX22190 CRC guideline (initial word 00111, polynomial 110101), pinned by golden vectors from ADI's reference code; not yet confirmed on silicon.

sourceFlags.note: bits above 3 (WBE and reserved) are not settable via source_flags; chip startup writes the board default 0x04 (1.6 ms, filter active) to FLT1..FLT4, then each channel's start writes its own value

drivers.name: ips2050
drivers.wiring: RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 IPS2050HTR protected high-side digital-output frontend, DO0/DO1. Plain GPIO frontend, no SPI/I2C/UART bus at all -- dedicated DOx_CMD/DOx_FAULT GPIO pins per channel plus a shared DO_ENABLE_REQ line (asserted once, on the first channel to start). See HARDWARE_MVP.md section 3.4.4.

sourceIndex.note: DO0/DO1, a 0-based renumbering of the schematic's 1-based DO1/DO2

sourceFlags.note: no per-channel configuration exists on this board -- polarity and safe-state wiring are fixed in hardware

drivers.name: uic
drivers.wiring: RP2350_INDUSTRIAL_MVP_V1 universal protected input channels UIC0..UIC3 (GPIO40..GPIO43), behind a TLV9034PWR quad push-pull comparator frontend (active-low: UICx_IN is LOW when the field input is active). Counter-based modes use RP2350 PIO (uic_pulse_counter.pio, one state machine per active channel); digital-input mode reads the GPIO directly with no PIO involved. Quadrature-encoder mode (ROADMAP.md/HARDWARE_MVP.md 'using channel pairs') is not implemented -- deliberately deferred, see docs/releases/v0.5.1.md T6.

sourceFlags.note: bits above 2 must be 0; mode 4 (quadrature) is not defined

defaultChannelTemplate.note: the correct kind/valueType/unit depend on the selected mode -- see modeChannelTemplates below, not a single fixed default

drivers.name: synthetic
drivers.wiring: None -- no external hardware dependency of any kind. Each channel counts its own read() calls independently, starting from 0 at start(), wrapping modulo 2^32. An exact integral FLOAT/DOUBLE write updates only that channel's loopback counter/runtime value; the next read continues at +1. ROADMAP.md's generic 'synthetic benchmark source'/'loopback... source for host tests' driver, and this project's minimal standalone example driver (ROADMAP.md:587, v0.5.1 T16) -- see drivers/include/drivers/synthetic_driver.h and docs/code/adding-a-driver.md.

sourceIndex.note: eight independent synthetic channels so several can be configured at once without interfering
